question_type: max over three calendar-year-ends of a ratio of two rows of one table (currency share of total liabilities to foreigners), unpinned vintage, rounded decimal
decisive_step: Which table holds 'Canadian dollar liabilities' and 'total liabilities to foreign countries' together: the bank-reported Capital Movements table CM-I-1 'Total Liabilities by Type and Holder' (rows 'Total liabilities to all foreigners' and, under 'Payable in foreign currencies > Major currencies:', 'Canadian dollars'; millions of USD; one 'Calendar Year YYYY' column per issue) rather than the Foreign Currency Positions tables FCP-I-2/FCP-I-3 ('Canadian Dollar Positions', millions of CAD, reporting market participants only), IFS-2 (header literally 'Liabilities to foreign countries' but no currency rows) or CM-III-1 (same row layout but nonbanking enterprises). The reference solver made it at worklog.md Step 3 (grep hit at treasury_bulletin_2012_03.txt:2240 inside CM-I-1) and solution.json decisions[0]; its adversarial reviewer then overrode it to CM-III-1 on a single-table/year-span coincidence (review.md section 3), which is why the reference is graded wrong. Once CM-I-1 is chosen, every vintage gives the same rounded answer (worklog Step 7), so vintage and rounding are not decisive here.

The fifth, [12] 'liabilities payable in Canadian dollars' --rows, returned exactly CM-I-1, CM-III-1 and CM-IV-1 (match:tokens). show_table on CM-I-1 ([14] --grep '2009' matched nothing; [16] page 1 = 9 of 39 rows, ended before the currency rows), then a raw sed [20] showed the 'Payable in foreign currencies' / 'Canadian dollars' rows. printings [22]-[26] for both rows in each 'Calendar Year 2009/2010/2011' column across issues, took the latest printing of each, calc [28] for the three ratios, the max and the rounding.

smallest_change.change: find_tables: search row labels by default and match tokens by prefix. In otables.py find_page(), build the FTS query over '{title header rowlabels}' always (drop the --rows opt-in, keep the flag as a no-op) and emit each token as a prefix term ('"canadian"* AND "dollar"* AND "liabilit"*' for tokens of 4+ chars), or rebuild the index with tokenize='porter unicode61'. Add 'rowlabels' to the where/match column and print the matched row labels in the group line. Verified against v9-p1-a/prepared/agent/tables/tables.sqlite: today's query for 'Canadian dollar liabilities' (used verbatim by b[8], b2[8], c[7], a[10]) returns only FCP-I-2/FCP-I-3 with or without --rows, because CM-I-1's label is the plural 'Canadian dollars' and unicode61 has no stemming; with rowlabels + prefix the same query returns CM-I-1 and CM-III-1 as well. The model would have seen, at b[8]/b2[8]/c[7], two extra group lines such as: '[CM-I-1] Total Liabilities by Type and Holder  | 51 issues 2001_06..2013_12 | match:rowlabels (Total liabilities to all foreigners; Canadian dollars)' and '[CM-III-1] Total Liabilities and Claims by Type  | 28 issues 2006_12..2013_12 | match:rowlabels (Total liabilities; Canadian dollars)'.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a already used --rows; ranking stays title > header > tokens so title/header hits still lead; the only cost is longer lists for one-word queries, which the existing 8000-byte cap and --years already handle. Residual risk: with CM-I-1 and CM-III-1 both listed, a cell could pick CM-III-1 (the reference's reviewer did), so the fix makes the right table visible rather than certain.

alternatives.change: A 'grep rows' capability: find_tables --rows prints, per hit, the row labels that matched (e.g. rows: 'Canadian dollars' under 'Payable in foreign currencies'), so the model sees the fit without paging through show_table (a[14]-[16] needed a raw sed to see the currency rows).

notes: (1) show_table --grep is a substring filter on row label/period/section, not on column headers and not a regex: a[14], b[26]/[29], b2[14] each lost a step to it; the usage line should say so or the tool should accept a regex and also match column labels. (2) Multi-query commands lose output to the 8000-byte cap (b[8], b2[23], c[23]): README could say one query per command, or the cap could apply per query. (3) rg over the corpus for 'liabilit.*Canadian dollar' is useless here because the FCP header line contains both words ('Liabilities (4)' ... 'Exchange rate (Canadian dollars per U.S. dollar)'), so all three wrong cells got hundreds of header lines and no CM-I-1 row; a row-label index (the proposed find_tables change) is the right substitute for raw grep. (4) CM-I-1 prints only one 'Calendar Year' column per issue, so the three year-ends need three issues; a's printings --col 'Calendar Year 2009' handled this cleanly, and the tool's SUMMARY split 'Calendar Year 2009 r' and 'Calendar Year 2009' into two keys (a[22]) without confusing a. (5) Every vintage of CM-I-1 rounds to the same answer (reference worklog Step 7), so the latest-printing rule was harmless here; on this question the whole outcome is table discovery.
